problem: Semantic visual-navigation policies (RGB encoder to action) need large datasets and generalize poorly to unseen environments, while hybrid methods rely on ground-truth or noisy depth from RGB-D sensors and suffer sim-to-real gaps.
motivation: Traditional planners operate on geometric occupancy representations that are robust to appearance domain gaps, but need accurate geometry. Learning an explicit geometric representation from cheap stereo RGB and conditioning the policy only on it could give data efficiency, better generalization and real-time speed without any GT depth.
key_idea: Predict an auxiliary 3D voxel occupancy grid from stereo RGB with StereoVoxelNet, extract geometric features from it, and train a simple MLP policy on those features plus the goal, using modular then end-to-end training.
insight: Conditioning the policy on explicit geometry instead of semantic features improves success and generalization: SNN loses only 1% SR from seen to novel scenes versus 5% for ResNet, and beats depth-map hybrids at far lower compute. Modular pretraining matters: without it SR drops from 35% to 22%, because a randomly initialized perception module gives the policy noisy input. Grid resolution matters too (GT grid SR 52% at 64^3, 39% at 16^3, 22% at 4^3).
method: Perception module: StereoVoxelNet (2D-3D encoder-decoder) maps left/right stereo images directly to a robot-centric 64x64x64 binary occupancy grid, trained with IoU loss.
Geometric feature extractor: four 3D conv layers (kernel 4, stride 2, ReLU) turn the grid into a 256-d obstacle feature h_o.
Goal encoding: point goal (d, cos θ, sin θ) is encoded by a non-linear layer into a 16-d feature h_g.
Policy module: a four-layer MLP with BN and ReLU predicts a continuous velocity (v, ω); reactive and Markovian with no memory; trained by behavior cloning with MSE.
Modular learning: train perception for 150 epochs, then policy for 50 epochs on GT perception, then joint fine-tune for 300 epochs with L = L_p + 0.1 L_o.
Privileged expert data: A* on the global GT occupancy map plus a PD controller yields 500 demonstration trajectories (100 in each of 5 OmniGibson scenes) with domain-randomized lighting.

setting.backbone: StereoVoxelNet + 3D-conv feature extractor + 4-layer MLP (trained from scratch, behavior cloning)
setting.training_data: 500 expert trajectories (100 x 5 OmniGibson scenes), A* + PD controller privileged expert, 80/20 train/val split
setting.observation: stereo RGB (672x376) plus GT odometry / relative goal
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT odometry for the goal, as in PointNav); the privileged expert and GT voxel labels are used only in training

numbers_note: Values are printed as fractions (0.35) in the tables, whereas the text writes 35%; they are copied as printed. Each scene has 10 episodes. The custom OmniGibson PointNav benchmark is not one of the canonical names.
results: SNN reaches SR 35%, SPL 34% and NE 3.25 m over 13 scenes, beating MobileStereoNet (28/26/3.46) and Depth Anything (27/26/3.76) hybrids and the ResNet semantic baseline (SR 23%; novel-scene SR 21% vs SNN 35%). It runs in real time with 9.53G MACs and 1.15M params, versus 91G-300G MACs for the other hybrids.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation, so sim-to-real transfer is untested.
Reactive policy with no memory or mapping, and absolute success rates are low (about 35%).
Trained on only 500 trajectories from 5 scenes, with novel-scene tests limited to OmniGibson.
